liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **El Paso** (2 reviews): El Paso is sloppy, but the band recovers on Jack-a-Roe; El Paso was painfully slow, making the reviewer question Bob's choice of tempo [19][26]
- **Row Jimmy** (2 reviews): Row Jimmy was solid; Row Jimmy was the one first-set song that really popped for this reviewer [18][21]
- **Jack-A-Roe** (1 review): Jack-A-Roe was fairly rare for that period [18]
- **Lazy Lightning** (1 review): Lazy Lightning into Supplication was a happy surprise [26]
- **Supplication** (1 review): Nice Jerry jamming near the end of Supplication [19]
- **Scarlet Begonias** (1 review): Scarlet Begonias into Fire On The Mountain was very good [21]
- **Playing In The Band** (1 review): Playing in the Band is outstanding, in an early-1970s style [19]

## The recordings

- **gd1981-05-11.mtx.seamons.107252.flac16** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 24 songs; 183 min; rated 4.75/5 by 8 [1]
- **gd81-05-11.sbd.miller.30646.sbeok.flacf**: soundboard; 24 songs; 177 min; rated 3.5/5 by 8 [2]. Said about its sound: The Minglewood sounds like a patch from another, inferior source; Good but imperfect sound; reviewer guesses it was worse before Charlie Miller's remaster [21][24]
- **gd1981-05-11.175164.sbd.miller.remaster.flac1644**: soundboard; 24 songs; 176 min [3]
- **gd81-05-11.aud.unknown.4142.sbefail.shnf**: audience recording; 24 songs; 182 min; rated 4.5/5 by 8 [4]. Said about its sound: Reviewer calls this audience recording one of the best auds in the archive, immersive, like being there; The crowd is audible at times, but the music drowns it out [20]
- **gd1981-05-11.149197.fob.nak700.wagner.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 24 songs; 184 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [5]

## Around the show

- Reviewer attended as a high school senior, in section 13, row 22, seat 5 [16]
- Reviewer says they were at the show [22]
- Reviewer imagines the Yale students in the crowd loved the energetic show [23]
- Reviewer drove down from URI, arrived just in time, and stood front row backstage [26]
- Reviewer judges it the best show of the spring 1981 tour for both performance and audience-recording sound [16]
- Reviewer calls 1981 an overlooked year, with Brent settled in and the band gelling as a unit [18]
- Reviewer says 1981 is often overlooked next to 1977 and earlier, and 1989-1991 [22]
- First set weak, second set better, and many superior shows exist from this period [24]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1981-05-11.mtx.seamons.107252.flac16**: transferred by Hunter Seamons; source: Matrix using Final Cut Pro (FLAC > AIFF > Final Cut > AIFF CD tracking via Audacity > FLAC16 via xACT) [1]
- **gd81-05-11.sbd.miller.30646.sbeok.flacf**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Soundboard [2]
- **gd1981-05-11.175164.sbd.miller.remaster.flac1644**: transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  November 18, 2025; source: SBD > Cassette Master > Reel > DAT [3]. Also: Remaster of shnid 30646 from a source DAT supplied by Rob Eaton; The remaster repaired a vocal phase problem and swapped channels [3]
- **gd81-05-11.aud.unknown.4142.sbefail.shnf**: source: Audience Recording [4]
- **gd1981-05-11.149197.fob.nak700.wagner.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Bob Wagner; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Bob Wagner's Master (FOB) Audience Cassette; Nakamichi CM700 mics > Sony TC-D5M [5]. Also: Patches come from the shnid 4142 audience source and Frank Streeter's Nakamichi 700 front-of-board recording, in Minglewood, It's All Over Now and Drums [5]

## Art and photos

- Poster by @donelichterman: [Dead Set Live Presents: Don's Pick – The Grateful Dead Live at Veterans Memorial Coliseum, New Haven – May 11, 1981 - Th](https://thegratefuldeadlive.com/dead-set-live-presents-dons-pick-the-grateful-dead-live-at-veterans-memorial-coliseum-new-haven-may-11-1981/) [28]
